## Detailed entries

### Aberdeen

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-07-20 (City Council first reading and passage, 7-0)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-07-20` (exact)
- **Duration:** From adoption (immediate effect) through a fixed sunset of November 18, 2026, or the effective date of a zoning ordinance amendment addressing data centers, whichever occurs first
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `sd-aberdeen-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Resolution No. 26-07-04R, 'A Temporary Resolution Establishing a Moratorium on Issuance of Local Permits for Data Centers Within the City of Aberdeen,' adopted 7-0 at a regular Aberdeen City Council meeting on 2026-07-20, under authority of SDCL Sec. 49-50-3 (effective 2026-07-01)
- **What prompted it:** City's current zoning/building regulations and staff may not adequately address data centers; council found officials 'hampered' in assessing permit applications, creating unpredictability and risk of stranded investment pending a comprehensive study
- **Affected projects:** None named; as of publication Aberdeen had not received a specific data center development proposal for City Council consideration.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23. Resolution 26-07-04R (adopted 7-0 on July 20, 2026, published July 23, 2026) bars Aberdeen zoning and building officials from issuing any permit or license for the construction, development, or operation of a data center within city limits; any pending application is held without review or action. The resolution took immediate effect as an emergency measure under SDCL Sec. 9-19-13 and automatically expires and is repealed on November 18, 2026, or on the effective date of a zoning-ordinance amendment (Aberdeen City Code Chapter 60 - Zoning) addressing data centers, whichever is first. As of September 22, 2026, the City Attorney was still briefing the council on the timeline for that follow-on zoning ordinance, which had not yet been adopted.
- **Outcome:** Adopted 7-0 on first reading and passage at the July 20, 2026 regular City Council meeting; published July 23, 2026.

### Pennington County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2024-11-19 (Board of Commissioners unanimous vote); effective 2024-12-12; extended one additional year by unanimous vote on 2025-10-21
- **Normalized date:** `2024-11-19` (exact)
- **Duration:** One year from its December 12, 2024 effective date; extended unanimously on October 21, 2025 through November 18, 2026
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** wind, solar
- **Moratorium ID:** `sd-pennington-county-2024`
- **Legal basis:** Pennington County Board of Commissioners temporary zoning moratorium on utility-scale wind and solar development, adopted unanimously November 19, 2024 (effective December 12, 2024); extended unanimously October 21, 2025 through November 18, 2026, while an alternative-energy task force and the Planning Commission draft amendments to zoning ordinance Section 3-17 (renewable energy systems)
- **What prompted it:** More than 450 citizens petitioned for a moratorium after the Planning and Zoning Commission approved conditional-use permits (2024-10-28) for the Cheyenne River Ranch Wind and Solar Farm near New Underwood
- **Affected projects:** Cheyenne River Ranch Wind and Solar Farm (7 miles south of New Underwood, 30 miles southeast of Rapid City), which received conditional-use permit approval October 28, 2024 that triggered the petition and moratorium.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23. Pennington County's temporary zoning moratorium on utility-scale wind and solar development (enacted unanimously November 19, 2024, effective December 12, 2024, after 450+ citizens petitioned against the Cheyenne River Ranch Wind and Solar Farm's conditional-use permits) was extended unanimously by the Board of Commissioners on October 21, 2025 through November 18, 2026, to give an alternative-energy task force (formed March 2025) and the Planning Commission time to finish a consolidated ordinance amending zoning Section 3-17. A related but legally separate zoning-ordinance amendment permanently barring utility-scale wind and solar from agricultural (non-industrial) land passed its second and final reading 3-2 on August 18, 2026, after a multi-month back-and-forth (first reading May 19, 2026; delayed multiple times); commissioners indicated the moratorium could be lifted early once the Planning Commission's consolidated ordinance is finalized.
- **Outcome:** Extended by unanimous vote (moved by Commissioner Durr, seconded by Commissioner Rosknecht) at the October 21, 2025 Board of Commissioners meeting.

### Turner County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** On or about late August 2025 (news report dated 2025-08-27/28, 'Turner Co. OKs Wind Farm Pause'); exact Commission vote date not independently located in an archived primary source
- **Normalized date:** `2025-08` (month_only)
- **Duration:** Originally reported as a one-year moratorium on wind energy projects; county Board of Adjustment minutes from September and October 2025 describe a 'Moratorium on Solar and Wind Energy Systems' ordinance adopted by the County Commission, and a public-notice aggregator (not independently verified against an archived primary source) indicated a hearing was set for 2026-08-25 to consider extending a 'temporary moratorium on utility-scale alternative energy systems' county-wide.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** wind, solar
- **Moratorium ID:** `sd-turner-county-2025`
- **Legal basis:** Turner County Commission ordinance/resolution establishing a moratorium on wind (and later described as covering solar/utility-scale alternative energy) systems, adopted on or about August 2025; discussed at Turner County Board of Adjustment meetings on 2025-09-23 and 2025-10-21
- **What prompted it:** Proposed Swan Lake Wind Project (NextEra Energy Resources; up to 97 GE turbines, approximately 248 MW) spanning Turner and Yankton counties; county sought time to study and regulate before the project could proceed
- **Affected projects:** Swan Lake Wind Project (NextEra Energy Resources), spanning Turner and Yankton counties; NextEra withdrew its application for the project in or around August 2026.
- **Detailed status:** Status as of 2026-09-23 is only partially confirmed. Yankton.net reported (headline 'Turner Co. OKs Wind Farm Pause,' dated on or about 2025-08-27/28) that the Turner County Commission enacted a one-year moratorium on wind energy projects, putting the proposed Swan Lake Wind development on hold. Turner County Board of Adjustment minutes from 2025-09-23 confirm the Commission had adopted a 'Moratorium on Solar and Wind Energy Systems' ordinance and that the Board discussed forming a task force on it; minutes from 2025-10-21 show continued discussion of the 'Solar/Wind moratorium.' NextEra subsequently withdrew its wind-turbine application for the area (reported on or about 2026-08-21-28). A public-notice listing indicated Turner County scheduled an 8:35 a.m. public hearing on 2026-08-25 in Parker to consider extending a 'temporary moratorium on utility-scale alternative energy systems' county-wide, but the archived copy of that notice did not retain the underlying notice text (JS-rendered page returned only site boilerplate) and the outcome of any such hearing could not be confirmed from a source with retrievable primary text as of 2026-09-23. ### Yankton County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-07-21 (County Commission adopted the moratorium 5-0, recorded as Action 26248C)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-07-21` (exact)
- **Duration:** Six months from adoption (approximately to 2027-01-21); the commission packet draft had proposed 12 months, but the adopted motion changed the term to six months
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center, cryptocurrency mining
- **Moratorium ID:** `sd-yankton-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Yankton County Commission motion (Action 26248C), adopted 5-0 on July 21, 2026, following a July 10 public notice initially referenced as 'Ordinance 26-08'; final ordinance or resolution numbering was not confirmed
- **What prompted it:** Concern about incoming data center and Bitcoin mining facility proposals; commission wants time to draft permanent siting standards
- **Affected projects:** None named; general countywide pause on new data center and greater-than-250kW Bitcoin mining permits and applications.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of the July 31, 2026 research date. Blocks applications and permits for building, use, zoning, or rezoning approval of data collection, storage, or processing facilities and Bitcoin mining facilities exceeding 250 kW, for six months from the July 21, 2026 adoption. The commission separately directed the Planning and Zoning Commission to begin drafting permanent standards.
- **Outcome:** Enacted six-month moratorium after an initial motion for a 12-month term failed for lack of a second.
